newsitem.title: UK: Physical sugar - Thai raw premiums slide.
newsitem.headline: Physical sugar - Thai raw premiums slide.

text.p: Premiums for next year's Thai raw sugar crop have started to slide and are expected to fall further as the delivery period for New York's March futures contract approaches, physical sugar brokers said on Friday.
Cargoes of Thai raws for March/May delivery were recently quoted at premiums close to 75 points bid after 115 a few weeks ago and traded this week at 80 points bid, they said.
"Thailand sugars are on the slide," said one broker.
"The general view is that the Chinese will buy, March will be squeezed in New York and will drag down what sugars are available," he said.
Premiums for January/March and May/July cargoes both lost ground and were quoted at 110 and 108 points respectivley.
If Thai cargoes are dragged forward by demand for nearby deliveries, sugars for July delivery are likely to develop a scarcity value with correspondingly firm premiums, traders said.
July premiums were quoted at 150 points over New York.
While China's known buying requirement -- estimated at between 1.5 and 2.0 million tonnes -- has been factored into the market, questions over its timing have affected Thai premiums.
Brokers said China is not expected to buy before the end of February 1997, thus depressing prices for January and February Thai sugars, which are now quoted at 105 and 110 point premiums.
"China is probably going to be a two million tonne buyer next year, which will not have an effect on premiums," the broker said.
"What it will do is to give power to whoever sells to go long of the futures market and receive Thais at flat -- the general view is that March Thais will go to flat."

Earlier this month, Chinese authorities ordered sugar mills in major producing areas to reserve 300,000 tonnes of sugar this year -- the first time ever -- to boost slumping prices after large-scale smuggling sent prices plunging.
Now the internal price has risen, brokers say it could be tempting for locals to import sugar to sell it domestically.

But in the meantime Chinese buying is absent and regional demand is expected to remain tight until December, although countries such as Indonesia and the Philippines were active buyers of Thai raws earlier in the year, market sources said.
Availability of raw sugar for delivery against the New York March contract will be a major determining factor affecting physical prices for Thai cargoes.

While Thailand will be the principal origin to be tendered against the expiry, some central American sugars should also be available and there may be some north Brazil cargoes after the main shipments finish from the current crop.
"Brazil is depending on the differential between October and March but they still have a large quantity unpriced," said a trader with a Japanese trade house.
"The big imponderable in the market is Brazil and that's going to drag the market down in the near term," said another broker.
While Cuban sugars may not be delivered against any New York raws contract, the new crop will come on stream in December and cargoes can still be swapped against other origins.
"Cuban sugar will become available in December and it can be swapped," the trader said.
"So it's not so easy to predict that the only candidate for the March delivery is Thailand as some central American sugars are also available," he added.
